sources.title: Introducing Mercury 2.5
sources.evidence: Exact-model announcement identifies Mercury 2.5 as an Inception diffusion LLM, with 260K context, tunable reasoning, parallel tool calls and structured JSON. It offers hosted access via Inception API, Baseten and OpenRouter; no public checkpoint or numerical parameter count is provided. Freshly reopened October 27: the largest-diffusion-model statement is qualitative, qualified as to the developer’s knowledge, and contains no numeric total or active count. The same serving profile and production-feedback training narrative do not identify an unchanged sized base.

sources.title: Blog — Mercury 2.5 dated release entry
sources.evidence: The official index labels Introducing Mercury 2.5 as September 8, 2026 and links directly to the release announcement.

sources.title: Models
sources.evidence: Current model table explicitly lists Mercury 2.5 with 260K context, 65,536 maximum output tokens, text format, tool calling and structured outputs. Its named example uses mercury-2.5 and reasoning_effort. Fresh current exact-model row reopened October 27; it reports serving limits and capabilities, with no weight-count field.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.evidence: The FAQ explicitly names Mercury 2.5 among models accepting only text input and says image generation is unsupported.

sources.title: Reasoning Efforts
sources.evidence: Explicitly applies reasoning_effort to mercury-2.5; documents instant, low, medium and high, with medium as this model's default.

sources.title: Terms of Use
sources.evidence: Inception retains ownership of its services and grants restricted, non-transferable service-use rights. This supports a proprietary service classification, not an open model-weight license.

sources.title: Diffusion at Scale: Introducing Mercury 3
sources.evidence: Later October 19 announcement explicitly compares Mercury 2.5 and Mercury 3, retaining the former's 260K context. Its scaling chart names M2.5 but provides only total-parameter ratios relative to Mercury 1 Mini; it gives no absolute Mercury 2.5 count or active count. Freshly reopened October 27. The more-than-40-times total-parameter statement explicitly compares Mercury 3 with Mercury 1 Mini, not Mercury 2.5; no unchanged-checkpoint relationship is asserted.

sources.title: Model Quality vs. Model Size — five Mercury generations
sources.evidence: Viewed original chart linked by the Mercury 3 announcement. The M2.5 point is dated September 2026; horizontal axis is total parameters relative to Mercury 1 Mini on a logarithmic scale. No absolute billions, exact numerical M2.5 ratio, active parameters, or dense/MoE structure are stated. Re-fetched and visually inspected the original chart October 27. M2.5 is plotted near M2 on the relative-size axis; closeness is not exact equality and no absolute reference size is supplied.

sources.title: Mercury: Ultra-Fast Language Models Based on Diffusion
sources.evidence: Original June 2025 report describes Mercury Coder Mini and Small using Transformer denoisers. It does not name Mercury 2.5 or disclose a count for it; its earlier architecture and context details cannot establish this later exact variant. Freshly reopened and checked the full original text October 27, including architecture, fine-tuning and scaling sections. Mini and Small have no published absolute counts here, so neither can anchor the later ratio plot. Generic compatibility with fine-tuning is not a statement of Mercury 2.5’s base lineage.

sources.title: Research
sources.evidence: First-party publication index links the original Mercury report and founders' diffusion research. No Mercury 2.5 model card, parameter table, or exact-model dense/MoE disclosure appears in this index. Fresh October 27 index still links the June 2025 Mercury report plus other diffusion research, but no later exact Mercury 2.5 parameter disclosure.

sources.title: Inception API OpenAPI specification
sources.evidence: The mercury-2.5 ModelObject example gives context_length 260000, text input/output, and tools/structured-output support. Its created timestamp is duplicated across different generations and is not reliable release-date evidence. Downloaded schema establishes documentation, not a successful live model inference.

sources.title: AI BENCHY Mercury 2.5 Preview parameter estimate
sources.evidence: Freshly investigated the concrete approximately 100B search lead October 27. The page explicitly labels the value estimated, acknowledges Inception has not disclosed the count, and says it follows the Mercury 2 family record. Its parameter-source link opens Inception’s generic homepage, which gives no such count. It is not an original parameter measurement or documented unchanged-base inference and is not adopted for the production Mercury 2.5 record.

name.note: Exact public model name; API identifier mercury-2.5.

developer.note: Official developer announcement and API ownership.

family.note: Official announcements explicitly place the model in the Mercury succession.

release_date.note: Official blog index dates the production release announcement September 8, 2026. The shared created value in API examples is not a model-specific release timestamp.

open_weights.note: Published access is through proprietary hosted services; the checked official release, docs and research index provide no public Mercury 2.5 weight release. This is a distribution classification, not a claim that private deployment is impossible.

license.note: Descriptive classification of restricted Inception service access. No open model-weight license is published in the checked exact-model sources.

parameters_b.note: October 27 fresh exact-model total-parameter, billion-scale, technical-report and named-base searches found no supported nominal count. Reopened the exact launch/docs, later Mercury 3 comparison and original research index; checked the full original Mercury paper and visually inspected the original scaling chart. The chart lacks an absolute Mini reference count, and its nearby M2/M2.5 positions do not establish unchanged weights. The launch’s largest-model wording is qualitative, not a numeric specification. Investigated the approximately 100B AI BENCHY lead: it is expressly an estimate inherited from an unsized family record, not a disclosed count. Retain null because published count evidence is absent, not because an exact tensor census is unavailable.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-parameter searches separately checked exact-model research, arXiv, developer and model-comparison sources. No original table, plot or model card supplies an active count for Mercury 2.5. The later developer plot expressly measures relative total parameters; API request parameters, throughput and pricing are different quantities. No documented sized base or explicit active convention permits inheritance, and neither dense structure nor active-equals-total is assumed.

architecture.note: Exact-model announcement establishes diffusion. Dense versus MoE and a Mercury 2.5-specific internal network specification remain undisclosed in the sources checked; the original Coder Transformer report is not transferred to this variant.

context_window.note: Exact ModelObject value corroborates the advertised 260K context. The separate 65,536 output ceiling is not added to the context window.

modalities.note: Named API example lists both text input and output; FAQ explicitly excludes image input and generation for Mercury 2.5. Voice-agent uses do not establish native audio.

tool_call.note: Exact-model announcement supports parallel calls and API specifications list tools.

description.value: Diffusion language model for text chat, with adjustable reasoning effort, parallel tool calling, and structured outputs.
description.note: Replaces generic prose with documented exact-model behavior and adds the supported diffusion characterization.

patch.description: Diffusion language model for text chat, with adjustable reasoning effort, parallel tool calling, and structured outputs.
patch.notes: Inception has not published total or active parameter counts in the checked sources. Its later scaling chart gives relative total sizes without an absolute reference count. Dense versus MoE structure is also unspecified.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit checked the exact release and current docs, later developer scaling chart, original Mercury report, research index and fresh total/active/lineage searches. Absolute total and active counts remain undisclosed; the concrete approximately 100B web lead is expressly a family-based estimate, not a published specification. Explicit null patches preserve the unknowns. All twelve nonparameter assessments and earlier corrections are unchanged.
